title: Cost per successful task: benchmarking Kimi K3, GPT-5.5 and 8 more AI models
gist: Argues token price is the wrong signal for choosing a model; cost per successful task, counting retries and runs that hit the budget, is the right one. It measures the gap between perfect routing, a simple escalation ladder and blind escalation.
changes: Puts a ceiling and a floor on the model-choice lever. Perfect routing solves more tasks at a third of the cost of the best single model; careless escalation costs twice as much as any single model.
caveats: A vendor-partnered study on 40 tasks chosen where models disagree, which flatters routing. The agent is a thin loop with no prompt-cache or long-context effects.

numbers.metric: Cost per success with hindsight-perfect routing
numbers.baseline: $0.636 and 25 of 40 for the best single model

numbers.metric: Cost per success with naive escalation through every model

bears_on.note: The headroom is real and large, and a bad policy is worse than none.
